problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $x\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ given by

$$
x\operatorname{sin}⁡x={x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{6}}{5!}-\frac{{x}^{8}}{7!}+⋯
$$

using sigma notation.
worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & ={x}^{2} \\ {a}_{1} & =-\frac{{x}^{4}}{3!} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{{x}^{6}}{5!} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{{x}^{8}}{7!}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{(-1)^{0}{x}^{2\cdot (0+1)}}{(2\cdot 0+1)!} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{(-1)^{1}{x}^{2\cdot (1+1)}}{(2\cdot 1+1)!} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}{x}^{2\cdot (2+1)}}{(2\cdot 2+1)!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(-1)^{3}{x}^{2\cdot (3+1)}}{(2\cdot 3+1)!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2(n+1)}}{(2n+1)!}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2(n+1)}}{(2n+1)!}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
